subject: Re: GCP private offer - migrating commit across SKUs / migration strategy
messages:
From: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer commit - need to shift some of our commit between SKUs

Hi Evelyn,

Quick note from procurement: we're reclassifying several workloads ahead of Q4 and need to move ~40% of our committed spend on the current GCP private offer from the general 'inference' SKU to the new 'batch-inference-optimized' SKU. Our finance team wants a clear runbook for the drawdown and any timing/ invoicing implications so we don't miss our redemption windows.

Questions:
- Can Redwood support reallocating commit across SKUs within the same private offer, or do we need a new private offer?
- What is the expected timeline (how long for GCP to reflect changes once we submit paperwork)?
- Any impact to our current drawdown scheduling / invoice dates?

We have a PO in place and prefer to avoid a full re-onboarding. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Derek
Derek Shaw
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Enterprise
attachments: acme_po_2026_q3.pdf
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer commit - need to shift some of our commit between SKUs

Hi Derek — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: in many cases we can move committed spend between compatible SKUs inside the same private offer, but it depends on the SKU mapping that GCP has and whether the new SKU is allowed inside your existing private offer terms. If GCP requires a new private offer we can still avoid a full product re-onboarding; there is an administrative flow to migrate commitments that usually takes 2–3 weeks, but invoice timing and redemption windows need coordination.

Proposed next steps (I can own coordination):
1) I will run a quick SKU-compatibility check with GCP Marketplace Ops to confirm whether 'batch-inference-optimized' can be hosted under your current private offer.
2) If it can, we will produce a commit transfer matrix (who/which SKUs, amounts, effective date) and submit the amendment to GCP.
3) If not, we will prepare a scoped private-offer swap plan + timeline and indicate any changes to invoice triggers.
4) I'll loop in our Sales Ops (Jonas) and Partner Ops (Marissa) to align on billing and co-sell implications.

I attached a draft CSV layout for the transfer matrix (commit_transfer_matrix.csv) and a short summary PDF of how we handle drawdowns/invoice phasing. Can you confirm the % to move and preferred effective date (we usually try to align to the start of a billing period to minimize proration).

If helpful, I'm available Fri 11am–2pm PT for a quick 20-min sync.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Marissa / Derek — short status update from Sales Ops after a quick sync with GCP Marketplace Ops:
- GCP confirmed that SKU reassignments within the same private offer are permitted when the two SKUs map to the same product family and the private offer terms don't explicitly lock SKU IDs. 'Batch-inference-optimized' looks like a compatible variant in the same family, but GCP requires a signed amendment that lists the exact SKU IDs and the new effective allocation.
- Estimated processing time once GCP receives a complete amendment package: 10 business days.
- Invoice timing: GCP will apply the new SKU mapping prospectively from the effective date on the amendment. Any partial month proration will follow GCP's standard billing; if Acme wants to avoid proration we recommend setting the effective date to the first day of next billing month (we suggested Oct 1 in the call).

Action items for Acme (to get to a complete submission):
- Finalized commit_transfer_matrix.csv with: old_sku, new_sku, monthly_commit_amount_usd, effective_date, PO_reference
- Signed signature page for the PO amendment (DocuSign link below if you want to sign electronically).

I'll draft the amendment once we have the matrix and signature and route to GCP. Happy to run a short review with Acme before submission.

Jonas Weber
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
